question: Ktoré slovenské mesto pre jeho neobvykle veľa kostolov a veží prezývajú „malý Rím“?
source_excerpt: Because of the many churches within its city walls, Trnava has often been called "Little Rome" (Slovak: Malý Rím, Latin: parva Roma)

extra.why_interesting: Many Slovaks have heard the nickname but never stopped to think which town carries it or why. The church-spires clue gives a reasoning path, and Rome as a symbol of churches makes the answer satisfying.
extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia and Slovak sources confirm Trnava is nicknamed 'Malý Rím' for its many churches; no conflicting claimant or newer development found (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trnava).

explanation: Trnava mala v historickom centre toľko kostolov, že si vyslúžila prezývku slovenský Rím. Navyše tu celé stáročia sídlili ostrihomskí arcibiskupi, keď Turci obsadili Ostrihom.

question: Ktoré slovenské mesto sa pre svoje bane prezýva „zlaté mesto“ a dodnes sa v ňom razia slovenské euromince?
source_excerpt: Mincovňa Kremnica, š. p. sériovú razbu slovenských eurových mincí.

extra.why_interesting: Players may think of a 'golden town' as just a poetic label. The mint hint gives them a way to reason to the answer, and the payoff is that the euro coins in their own pocket come from that town.
extra.verification_notes: Kremnica mint began serial production of Slovak euro coins in 2008 and continues minting circulation coins (2024); Kremnica is the gold-mining town. Source: https://nbs.sk/_img/documents/_publik_nbs_fsr/biatec/rok2008/biatec_9_2008.pdf

explanation: Kremnické zlaté dukáty patrili v stredoveku k najcennejším minciam v Európe. Tamojšia mincovňa razí peniaze nepretržite už takmer sedem storočí, takže euro vo vašej peňaženke pochádza z rovnakej dielne ako dukáty kráľov.
